extracted.intended_audience: researchers, philanthropists, science-policy readers, and people interested in new research org models
extracted.subtask_description: Characteristics and design principles for Focused Research Organizations (FROs) as described by Convergent Research — i.e., how FROs are structured, funded, and what kinds of research/projects they pursue. Useful for designing or evaluating FRO-style entities or philanthropic research incubators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify high-impact scientific or technological R&D fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Convergent Research is designed to identify high-impact scientific or technological R&D fields.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The organization’s role is to spot fields with potential for major impact as the starting point for launching targeted efforts (e.g., through FROs). This is an explicit upstream selection criterion for where to deploy resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Launch organizations/ventures to address selected fields
rubrics_metrics.description: After identifying high-impact fields, Convergent Research launches companies (or organizations) to address these fields with a structure called Focused Research Organizations (FROs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model links field identification directly to creating mission-focused entities (FROs) rather than only funding dispersed academic projects; operationalizing selection by creating purpose-built organizations is part of the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit legal/organizational form for FROs
rubrics_metrics.description: A Focused Research Organization is a type of non-profit organization designed to address technical problems or perform scientific research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The FRO model emphasizes operating as non-profits (at least initially), distinguishing them from for-profit startups; legal/organizational form is part of what defines an FRO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Medium-to-large teams with corporate structures
rubrics_metrics.description: FROs have medium-to-large size teams with corporate structures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unlike small academic labs, FROs are organized with larger teams and corporate-like management/structure, implying different hiring, project management, and governance expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue projects unlikely to yield publishable results
rubrics_metrics.description: FROs embrace projects which are unlikely to yield publishable results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model explicitly tolerates or targets work not primarily aimed at academic publications — focusing on technical goals or product-like deliverables rather than traditional academic outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-disciplinary collaboration among scientists and engineers
rubrics_metrics.description: FROs frequently involve scientists and engineers collaborating across disciplines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interdisciplinary teamwork is a defining operational criterion; FROs deliberately combine expertise across fields to solve technical problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not initially profitable (distinct from startups)
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike a startup company, a FRO project is not profitable enough in its initial stages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The expectation of limited early financial returns distinguishes FRO projects from commercial startups and informs funding models (philanthropic/supportive rather than venture-return-driven early on).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pursue specific technical goals rather than general research
rubrics_metrics.description: Unlike think tanks or research institutes, FROs tend to pursue specific technical goals rather than general research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FROs are mission- and goal-oriented with narrowly defined technical deliverables or milestones, rather than broad, exploratory agendas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lifecycle: evolve into traditional non-profits or transition to startups/VC backing after goals met
rubrics_metrics.description: Once their technical goals are achieved, FROs may evolve into more traditional non-profits, or become backed by venture capital and transform into startups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The model allows for staged transitions depending on outcomes — successful technical achievement can trigger organizational transformation or different funding sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address research bottlenecks / unblock technical roadblocks
rubrics_metrics.description: The model aims to unblock research bottlenecks with non‑profit start-ups (FROs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practical objective/metric for FRO success is whether it removes specific technical bottlenecks that impede progress in a field — i.e., solving concrete obstacles rather than producing incremental publications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Philanthropic/incubator funding model
rubrics_metrics.description: Convergent Research is an incubator for philanthropic ventures funded by donors (e.g., Eric Schmidt, Wendy Schmidt, Ken Griffin) as part of a broader network.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The funding model is philanthropic/incubator-driven rather than purely government grant or commercial VC early-stage funding; this shapes risk tolerance, time horizons, and expectations for returns.
